intro: British citizenship for spouses has a shorter route: if you’re married to or the civil partner of a British citizen, you can apply after 3 years’ residence, as soon as you have ILR.
cardText: A 3-year route for husbands, wives and civil partners of British citizens.

rules.title: Absence limits
rules.text: No more than 270 days outside the UK in the 3 years before you apply, and 90 days in the last 12 months. Use our [absence calculator](/absence-calculator/).

rules.title: Good character
rules.text: The Home Office checks criminal records, immigration history and debts.

boxTitle: Want a second pair of eyes before you apply?
boxText: A consultation costs far less than a refused application. We’ll check your case against the current rules and tell you honestly where you stand.

sections.heading: British citizenship for spouses: requirements
sections.text: You must be married to or the civil partner of a British citizen, hold ILR or settled status, have lived in the UK for at least 3 years with absences within the limits, pass the Life in the UK test, have B1 English and meet the good character requirement.

faqs.q: Do I need to wait 12 months after ILR?
faqs.a: No, not if you are married to a British citizen.

faqs.q: How many days can I be abroad?
faqs.a: No more than 270 in 3 years and 90 in the last 12 months.

faqs.q: Does my partner need to be British by birth?
faqs.a: No. They just need to be a British citizen.
